title: Daniyal Mansur, Founder and CEO of 22 Signals
description: Daniyal Mansur is the founder and CEO of 22 Signals in London. He built an esports company at 17, ran large live events and now builds AI systems.
h1: Daniyal Mansur, Founder and CEO of 22 Signals
intro: Daniyal Mansur is the founder and CEO of 22 Signals, a London business solutions company. He started his first company at 17, grew it to a million followers, helped run large live events, and now leads a team that moves businesses off the old way of working and onto intelligent systems.

p: Daniyal leads 22 Signals from London. He wins clients, sets the company's direction and runs its operations. He also still builds some of the company's AI tools himself, which keeps him close to what the team is actually delivering.
His focus is helping businesses move off the old way of working and onto intelligent systems. His LinkedIn headline puts it simply: "Helping ambitious companies lead the next era of business."

list: Paid campaigns run with budgets of up to $30,000 a month.
p: Across all of it, the aim is the same: replace manual, scattered ways of working with systems a business can rely on, then use them to grow.

sections.h: Salt Esports: starting a company at 17
p: Daniyal launched Salt Esports in 2019, at 17, and was its co-founder and CEO from 2019 to 2022. He grew it to 1 million followers and 50 million monthly impressions, and revenue grew 25 times between 2020 and 2022.

He brought in brand partnerships with Red Bull, Daraz, Unilever and Nayza; the Nayza deal was at the time the largest esports deal in Pakistan. Under his leadership Salt released eight apparel collections and launched Pakistan's first esports podcast.

The competitive side matched the commercial one. Salt's teams won more than 50 tournaments, and Salt was the first team from Pakistan at the Commonwealth Esports Championships in 2022. Daniyal was also the youngest founder in the Punjab IT Board's National Expansion Plan, Plan9.

From 2024 to 2025 Daniyal was a Strategy Consultant at Next Generation Esports. He helped run large-scale events for brands including Tencent, Garena and TCL, and Galaxy Racer 2024, which drew more than 20,000 attendees. He also built a corporate gamification unit there.

Live events taught him the lesson he now applies to every client project: the date doesn't move. A broadcast starts when it starts, whether or not everything is ready. That is why every date 22 Signals agrees with a client goes in writing.

Daniyal holds an MSc in Business Analytics with Distinction from Queen Mary University of London, completed in 2026. On the course he was team lead on a process-mining project in Celonis, analyzing an order-to-cash process.
Before that he earned a BBA (Hons) from the Lahore School of Economics, where he was President of the Entrepreneurship and Business Society from 2023 to 2025.
Daniyal Mansur spoke at Ten18 by Epiphany in 2023.

sections.h: How he thinks about the work
p: His path runs from building a brand and an audience, to running events where nothing can slip, to analyzing how businesses actually operate. It is also the mix 22 Signals is built on: AI, data, technology and marketing in one team, with one accountable lead. Most companies do not need more suppliers. They need someone who will own the result.
"Live events taught me that the date doesn't move," Daniyal says. "I run every client project the same way."

Daniyal Mansur is based in London and leads 22 Signals from its head office there. Companies that want to talk about moving their business onto intelligent systems can book a 15-minute call with the 22 Signals team.
